title: Data Sovereignty Onboarding — Triage & Ops Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational triage and checklist for onboarding customers with explicit data sovereignty or regional residency requirements. Focus is on decisions the private-deployments team must make during scoping, the minimal technical enforcement options, and an ops-friendly runbook for verification and ongoing compliance telemetry.

Audience:
- Solutions Eng / SEs doing presales and scoping
- Customer Success onboarding leads
- Private Deployments engineers and SREs
- Security & Compliance reviewers

High-level intake (what SE must capture before an internal kickoff):
1) Customer legal boundary statement (copy or region list they require). Example: "All customer PII and prompt history must remain within eu-west-1 and not be replicated outside."
2) Which product surfaces are in scope (hosted API, dedicated, private VPC, on-prem)?
3) Minimal required controls: geo-pin (hard), geo-preference (soft), egress-blocking, audit-level logging, KMS tenancy (customer-managed), HSM needed?
4) Expected traffic profile (tokens/day, burst TPS, average seq length) — impacts minimal deployment topology.
5) Any regulatory references: GDPR clause, Schrems II notes, local PA laws, sector (healthcare/finance).
6) Contractual SLA or audit windows (retention, incident notification time).
7) Legal/Privacy contact + SOC/Infosec reviewer names.

Decision matrix (technical levers and recommended defaults) :
- Soft pin (routing preference): route requests to preferred region if capacity available; if not, route to fallback and mark flagged in audit logs. Use when customer accepts functional equivalence and wants latency/cost flex. Default: NOT for high-assurance contracts.
- Hard pin (strict enforcement): requests for pinned account/route must only land on nodes with data locality guarantee; reject or return 403 if capacity unavailable. Required for "no cross-border replication" contracts.
- Local storage only: All artifacts (request logs, prompt history, embeddings) stored only in customer region. Requires storage-backed KV stores in-region and no async replication to global analytics.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed KMS recommended for enterprise/sovereign customers. If HSM required note lead time (procurement/integration).
- Network egress controls: L7 ACLs plus VPC routing to prevent accidental egress (egress IP allowlists).

Mapping to product capabilities (quick guide for SE):
- Hosted API: generally cannot meet hard pin; only recommend for soft-pin, non-sensitive workloads.
- Dedicated: supports region pinning via dedicated GPU pools; confirm capacity and isolation contractually.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): supports full hard pin and KMS/HSM integrations, but needs deployment plan and runbook.

Implementation checklist (pre-kickoff -> go-live):
Pre-kickoff (SE):
- Collect intake above and attach to ticket (PD-ONB-XXXX).
- Flag likely hard/soft requirement in ticket summary.
- Share initial capacity estimate with infra for feasibility.

Kickoff (cross-functional):
- Invite: SE, Solutions Eng, Infra Eng, SRE, Security, Customer Success, Delivery PM.
- Confirm jurisdiction map and dataset examples (what counts as regulated data).
- Confirm acceptable fallback behavior in outage window (reject vs. degrade).

Design decisions (engineering):
- Decide enforcement mode per route/account (hard|soft|off).
- Assign region tag in model-routing table and add validation to control plane API.
- Define audit fields: policy_id, enforcement_mode, routed_region, fallback_region, decision_timestamp, request_id.
- Telemetry: emit a residency_decision metric (labels: enforcement_mode, region, result) and residency_violation_counter.

Deployment tasks (runbook snippets):
- Provision dedicated pool in target region; ensure isolation label set: pool.metadata.residency=eu-west-1-customer-123
- Storage: create in-region bucket with versioning disabled if contract requires ephemeral logs; attach bucket policy to prevent global replication.
- KMS: create CMK under customer-managed key alias and configure runtime to fetch key via KMS alias. Document key rotation window.
- Network: verify VPC routing table and egress ACLs; ensure NAT gateways do not route to outside regions.

Verification & pre-cutover checks:
- Dry-run traffic: send test requests with header X-Residency-Account and monitor routing decisions in control plane logs.
- Generate compliance report: list of active nodes, storage endpoints, KMS keys, and IP blocks in use — deliver to SOC reviewer.
- Penetration checklist: confirm no cross-region backups, verify blocking of async analytics exports, and run list of allowed egress destinations.

Operational behavior and SLOs:
- If hard-pin enforced and capacity unavailable: configured behavior must be explicit in contract. Recommended: maintain emergency burst pool within same region or fail with clear error code 451 (or custom code).
- Telemetry SLO: residency-decision latency under 20ms for control plane calls.
- Alerting: residency_violation_counter > 0 triggers P1 to oncall and security.

Audit and logging guidance:
- Retain per-request residency audit logs for 365 days unless contract states otherwise. Store logs in-region encrypted with CMK.
- Log fields must include original client IP, routed node id, enforcement_mode, decision_reason, and any fallback_reason.
- Periodic signed attestations (quarterly) to customer summarizing no cross-border access and listing infra changes.

Common edge cases and suggested handling:
- Multi-tenant model weights: if customer requires all artifacts remain in-region, prefer serving with local copy of model weights rather than remote shared weights. Document cost/tradeoff.
- Cross-region async evals: forbid by default for hard-pin contracts; for soft-pin allow only if anonymization contractually approved.
- Backup & DR: backup copies allowed only in pinned region unless explicit exception is granted. Establish disaster recovery playbook that involves customer signoff for DR failover to other region.

Escalation playbook (if a residency violation is detected):
1) Immediate: auto-quarantine offending node and stop new requests for that account.
2) Notify oncall (SRE) + security + account owner.
3) Triage: collect request lineage, storage replication logs, and KMS access audit.
4) Remediation: roll policy changes, remove cross-region job, and restore from in-region snapshot.
5) Follow-up: postmortem within 72 hours and customer-facing incident report if data exposure is possible.

Open questions / decisions to finalize (team action items):
- Define canonical error codes for enforcement-mode failures (Ravi to propose by 2025-01-15).
- Decide maximum allowed failover window for hard-pin customers before invoking contractual SLA (legal + product).
- Telemetry retention policy alignment with privacy (Maya to sync with Privacy Counsel).

Quick templates (copy-paste for SE):
- Intake email subject: "Onboarding: Data Sovereignty Scope for <customer-name> — Regions: <list>"
- Required legal ask: "Please attach the Data Boundary Addendum and specify whether KMS must be customer-managed and whether any analytics exports are allowed off-region."

Appendix: useful commands and examples
- Control plane API sample to set enforcement mode:
  PATCH /control/v1/accounts/{acct}/residency
  body: {"enforcement_mode": "hard", "pinned_region": "eu-west-1"}

- Check routing decision via logs:
  gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name="pd-pool-eu-west-1" AND jsonPayload.account="acct-123"' --limit 50

Notes to self (informal):
- For mid-tier enterprise, soft-pin + CMK might be quickest sales win. Hard-pin is expensive but often required for public sector.
- Keep a small dedicated EU emergency pool (cost center) to reduce go-live friction for hard-pin customers.
- Need a short internal training deck for SEs showing canned Q&A.

References:
- Confluence DSO-templates (linked above)
- PD-1379 (JIRA) — previous customer case study with HSM integration
- Internal runbook: private-deployments/backup-and-replication-rules
